what: The hardware digests (runtime/c/bcir_digest_hw.c): SHA-256 on SHA-NI and CRC-32 by carry-less-multiply folding, against the portable code (bcir_sha256.c, bcir_crc32.h's slicing-by-8), each over 1 MiB 64 times, three runs: test_digest_hw --bench
host: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, 4 vCPU, a virtual machine (sha_ni, pclmulqdq, ssse3, sse4_1 in /proc/cpuinfo); Linux 6.18; gcc 13.3, -std=c11 -O2
tree: 8092ada3ad4ab8e79c1045ba8fd5660fe6f02185 plus the slice that adds bcir_digest_hw.c
method: clock() around 64 digests of one 1 MiB buffer per path, in one process; MB/s = 64 MiB / seconds. Process CPU time on a shared virtual machine: the wall class, INDICATIVE only and never a gate
not_measured: the ARMv8 SHA-2 and CRC32 paths (no AArch64 host here; CI's ubuntu-24.04-arm runner holds them to hashlib and zlib natively, not to a time), and short inputs, where the CRC's fold does not run (under 64 bytes) and the SHA-256 path takes only whole blocks
